name: Leg extension
pattern: Knee extension in isolation: seated, the lower leg swings up against resistance until the knee is straight.
setup: Sit back against the pad, knee joint in line with the machine's pivot.
Shin pad just above your ankle, toes pointing up.
Hold the handles to keep your hips down on the seat.

steps.text: Knees bent about 90°, weight just off the stack.
Straighten your knees smoothly by tightening your thighs.
Squeeze for a moment with the knee straight but not snapped.
Lower under control back to the start.

cues.cue: Line the knee up with the machine's pivot.
cues.why: A mismatched pivot drags the pad along the shin and shears the knee.

cues.cue: Hips stay down, back on the pad.
cues.why: Lifting the hips or swinging turns it into momentum, not quads.

cues.cue: Full lift to straight, slow lower.
cues.why: The quads work hardest near full extension in this open-chain move.

cues.cue: No swinging; pause 1-2 seconds at the top.
cues.why: Control keeps load on the muscle rather than the joint.

cues.cue: After knee surgery, use the range your therapist sets.
cues.why: ACL strain in this move is highest near a straight knee, so early rehab often keeps it to about 90-45° of bend.

breathing: Breathe out as you lift, in as you lower.

tempo.note: Lift in 1 second, hold 1, lower in 2.

mistakes.name: Hips lift and swing
mistakes.looks: The hips rise off the seat and the body jerks back to throw the weight.
mistakes.fix: Hold the handles, lighten the load, lift smoothly.
mistakes.why: Momentum and hip extension replace quad work.

mistakes.name: Stops short of straight
mistakes.looks: The knee never gets past about 30° bend at the top.
mistakes.fix: Use a weight you can fully straighten and hold.
mistakes.why: Misses the range where the quads work hardest.

mistakes.name: Weight drops
mistakes.looks: The stack crashes down and the knee jerks into deep bend.
mistakes.why: Skipping the lowering half wastes the eccentric work and jolts the knee.

safety: After ACL surgery, early leg extensions are usually limited to about 90-45° of knee bend; follow your therapist.
Knee-cap pain: try a shorter range, or squats and leg presses instead, which load the knee cap less near straight.
Never lock the knee hard against a heavy load.

variants.change: One leg at a time: same angles, half the load.
Band or ankle weight while seated on a chair: same keyframes, lighter.
Standing with a band: hip and knee start bent, then straighten the knee.
Isometric: hold the knee straight for 5-10 seconds.
Toes turned in a little; small shifts in quad activation only.

easier: seated knee extension with no weight

subtypes.name: Kneeling sissy squat
subtypes.change: Kneel upright, lean your straight body back from the knees, then pull back up with the quads.

subtypes.name: Sissy squat
subtypes.change: Standing on your toes, lean back from the knees with hips straight, knees travel forward and down, then rise. Kneeling version: lean back from the knees.

metrics.label: Knee bend
metrics.good: 90 at the start, 0-10 at the top

metrics.label: Hips off the seat (degrees of hip change)

motion.basis: Range (90° to straight) from escamilla1998 and wilk1996; seat back assumed reclined about 10° (estimate). Sissy squat angles estimated from the movement; no lab data found.
